rv.q: Invictus mostly succeeds in creating a world where the very air feels thick with desire and regret, the two inextricably knotted together.

“Any idiot can face a crisis,” Russian playwright Anton Chekhov wrote in one of his cheerier moods. “It’s this day-to-day living that wears you out.” Actually, the quote may belong to another dour playwright, Clifford Odets, but that hardly matters here.
Seize your Moscow and see Three Sisters.
For a smallish storefront theater like Invictus to do so well by a play as expansive and demanding as “Three Sisters” is no mean feat, and I wish the show a long and happy run.
Despite an uneven start and a few underperforming performances, Three Sisters delivers what audiences should expect from the classic drama.
It is a solid production that might be a little long for the average theater audience.

cn.t: Invictus Theatre Company tackles Chekhov's classic with ambition in an intimate setting, though the nearly three-hour production proves challenging. Critics find the faithful rendering of yearning and deferred dreams competent but taxing.
